topics: Volume & surface area of prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres

body.en: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume — from circles and trapezia up to cylinders, cones and spheres. Read each question carefully for the value of \( \pi \) it expects (often \( 3.14 \) or \( \tfrac{22}{7} \)).
Circumference \( C=2\pi r=\pi d \); area \( A=\pi r^{2} \). An arc and sector are simply fractions of these, scaled by \( \dfrac{\theta}{360} \).

body.en:
Find the volume of a cylinder with \( r=3 \) cm and \( h=10 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\pi r^{2}h=3.14\times 9\times 10=282.6\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]

Find the volume of a sphere of radius \( 3 \) cm. Take \( \pi=3.14 \).

\[ V=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}=\tfrac{4}{3}\times 3.14\times 27=113.04\ \text{cm}^{3}. \]

body.en:
Area & Volume Unit Conversions: Converting square and cubic units is a major Cambridge trap. \(1\text{ m}^2 = (100\text{ cm})^2 = 10,000\text{ cm}^2\), NOT 100! Similarly, \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1,000,000\text{ cm}^3\) and \(1\text{ litre} = 1,000\text{ cm}^3\).

Total Surface Area: For open-topped or hollow solids, omit missing faces. A closed cylinder has area \(2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\); a solid hemisphere has total surface area \(2\pi r^2 + \pi r^2 = 3\pi r^2\) (including the flat circular base).

Slant Height vs. Vertical Height: In cones and pyramids, \(h\) is the perpendicular vertical height and \(l\) is the slant height, linked by Pythagoras: \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2}\). The curved surface area of a cone uses \(l\) (\(\pi r l\)), while volume uses \(h\) (\(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\)).

label.en: Worked example 4.C — Sector Area & Arc Length

body.en:
A sector of a circle has radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\) and sector angle \(\theta = 120^\circ\). Calculate (a) the arc length and (b) the area of the sector, giving answers in terms of \(\pi\).

(a) Arc length: \(L = \frac{120}{360} \times 2\pi (6) = \frac{1}{3} \times 12\pi = 4\pi\text{ cm}\).

(b) Sector area: \(A = \frac{120}{360} \times \pi (6^2) = \frac{1}{3} \times 36\pi = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2\).

label.en: Worked Example D — Euclidean Distance & Orthogonal Projection

body.en:
A displacement has horizontal component \( \Delta x = 5 \) and vertical component \( \Delta y = 5 \). Find the squared magnitude \( d^2 \) and the area of the right triangle formed with the axes.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. By the Pythagorean theorem, \( d^2 = (5)^2 + (5)^2 = 25 + 25 = \mathbf{50} \).
  2. The enclosed right-triangle area is \( A = \frac{1}{2}(5)(5) = \mathbf{12.5} \).

question.en: A solid toy is formed by attaching a cone of radius 4 cm and height 9 cm to the flat face of a solid hemisphere of radius 4 cm. Calculate the total volume of the toy. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

solution.en:
Step 1: Volume of cone:

\[V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi (4^2)(9) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

Step 2: Volume of hemisphere:

\[V_{\text{hemi}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3}\pi (4^3) = \frac{128}{3}\pi\text{ cm}^3\]

Step 3: Total volume:

\[V_{\text{total}} = 48\pi + \frac{128}{3}\pi = \frac{272}{3}\pi \approx 284.838\dots \approx 285\text{ cm}^3\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

question.en: [Mensuration · Practice 2] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 4t + 4 \), evaluate \( g(6) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 32 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 6 \): \( g(6) = 4(6) + 4 = \mathbf{28} \). Setting \( 4t + 4 = 32 \) gives \( 4t = 28 \implies t = \mathbf{7} \).

question.en: [Mensuration · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Mensuration · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
